category: Usenet binary search engine (HTML search, anonymous NZB download)

free_tier.stated: No account and no key. GET /search/?q=linux returned 54,006 bytes with a rendered result list, and GET /nzb:<details-id>/ returned a 7,231-byte NZB with 19 files. No daily counter is published on the site.
free_tier.notes: No quota page exists; the claim rests on a 5-request burst rather than a vendor sentence.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the answer is an NZB pointer file (7,231 bytes, 19 files), never the payload

retention.stated: not stated on the pages read. A third-party indexer comparison claims '4,000+ days retention, 200 million+ Usenet posts indexed, 3,570 newsgroups' (nzbhydra.com, 2026-10-23).

egress.terms: No metering. The result page and the NZB are both kilobytes; the payload comes from the news provider.

interface_detail: HTML search over HTTP GET against /search/?q=<query>. Each result carries a /details:<id>/ link and an NZB link served as /nzb:<id>/. Both are plain GETs.
tooling: No Newznab API found, so Prowlarr and NZBHydra2 cannot add it. A wrapper parses /search and GETs /nzb:<id>/, and the site also offers a per-query RSS feed (the page advertises 'Get query as RSS feed'), which is the cheaper automation route.
chaining: A third unnamed fallback that also exposes an RSS feed per query, so a cron job can watch a name without a scraper.

limits.value: none observed: 5 consecutive anonymous searches in one session, all 200

limits_note: No request counter, byte counter or per-IP shaping was observed.
binding_note: Nothing in the vocabulary fails at 1 TiB/month. The practical ceiling is index coverage per newsgroup, which is not a limit kind.

identity_cost.detail: No account and no key: search and NZB download both answered an anonymous request.

reliability_note: The result page loads a cookie-consent script and an analytics tag before results; the results themselves are server-rendered, so a plain GET still sees them.
confidence_note: Search and download were run today with status, bytes and digest. A per-query RSS feed is advertised in the page text but was not fetched, so the feed route is documented-by-advertisement only.

evidence.proved: anonymous search returned 200 and 54,006 bytes with a rendered result table and per-result /details:<id>/ links
anonymous NZB download returned 200, application/x-nzb, 7,231 bytes, 19 <file> elements (sha256 a7308d72...)
no Newznab-style API path: 404, so a client cannot add it as an indexer
